outputs.L1: The present disclosure relates to a content recommendation method, device, and system. The method includes: recommending content from a content set to a user based on an average recommendation probability; collecting feedback information on the recommended content from the user’s client, wherein the feedback information includes display information and click information, the display information including display times and display timing of the recommended content on the client, and the click information including click times and click timing of the recommended content on the client; and determining a sequence of preferred content from the content in the content set according to the feedback information, so as to recommend content to the user based on the sequence of preferred content. Various aspects of the present disclosure recommend content based on user feedback, thereby enabling reasonable and effective content recommendation for random users who exhibit fewer click behaviors.
outputs.L2: This disclosure concerns a method, apparatus, and system for recommending content. The method involves selecting and presenting content from a content collection to a user according to an average recommendation probability; obtaining feedback data about the presented content from the user’s client, where the feedback data comprises display data and click data, the display data indicating the number of times the recommended content is shown on the client and the timing of those displays, and the click data indicating the number of times the recommended content is clicked on the client and the timing of those clicks; and, based on the feedback data, identifying an ordered list of preferred content items from the content collection, such that subsequent recommendations to the user are made according to that ordered list. The various aspects of this disclosure use user feedback as the basis for content recommendation, enabling suitable and effective recommendations even for random users with relatively few click actions.
outputs.L3:
The disclosure relates to a content recommendation method, device, and system designed to improve the effectiveness of recommending content to users, particularly in situations where user behavior data is limited.

In this approach, content is first selected from a content set and recommended to a user based on an average recommendation probability. This allows the system to provide an initial recommendation even when there is little or no prior information about the user’s preferences. Such an initial recommendation strategy is especially useful for random users or new users whose historical click behavior is insufficient for conventional recommendation models.

After the content is presented to the user, the system collects feedback information from the client. The feedback may include various types of interaction data, such as the number of times content is displayed, the timing of those displays, the number of times the user clicks on the content, and the timing of those clicks. By collecting both display-related and click-related information, the system obtains a broader understanding of how the user responds to different content items.

Based on the collected feedback information, the system determines a sequence of preferred contents from the content set. This sequence reflects the user’s likely interests and can be used to guide subsequent recommendations. Rather than relying only on explicit click behavior, the system takes into account additional feedback signals, such as exposure frequency and the timing relationship between content display and user interaction.

As a result, the disclosed method can provide more effective and personalized content recommendations, even for users who exhibit limited click behavior. By using a wider range of feedback signals, the recommendation system can better infer user preferences and improve the relevance of recommended content over time.
outputs.L4:
A content recommendation method, device, and system are provided for improving the accuracy and effectiveness of recommended content, particularly in situations where user behavior data is limited or where the user appears to browse randomly. In an initial recommendation stage, the system determines candidate content items and recommends the items according to an average recommendation probability. This allows content to be presented to a user even when there is not yet enough personalized historical data to build a reliable user preference model.

After the recommended content is displayed, the system collects feedback information associated with the user’s interaction with the content. The feedback information may include, for example, the number of times each content item is displayed, the number of times the content item is clicked, the time at which the content is displayed, the time at which the content is clicked, and other behavior data reflecting the user’s response to the recommendation. By analyzing both the exposure data and the click data, the system can determine whether a particular content item is more likely to be preferred by the user, rather than relying solely on simple click frequency.

Based on the collected feedback information, the system calculates or updates a preference ranking for the recommended content. Content items that receive stronger positive feedback, such as higher click-through performance or more favorable interaction timing, may be ranked higher and selected with greater priority in subsequent recommendation rounds. Content items with weaker feedback may be assigned a lower rank or reduced recommendation probability.

Through this process, the recommendation system gradually adjusts from an initial probability-based recommendation strategy to a feedback-driven personalized recommendation strategy. As a result, the system can provide more reasonable and effective recommendations even for users who have little historical behavior data, users who click infrequently, or users whose browsing behavior is relatively random. The method improves content matching efficiency, enhances user experience, and increases the likelihood that recommended content will satisfy the user’s actual interests.
outputs.L5:
**The Respective Roles of “The” and “Respective” in Language**

The words **“the”** and **“respective”** may seem simple, but they play important roles in making communication clear and precise. **“The”** is a definite article used to refer to something specific or already known. For example, when someone says, “the book,” they are not speaking about any book, but a particular one.

The word **“respective”** is used to show that two or more things belong or relate separately to the people or items already mentioned. For instance, “The students returned to their respective classrooms” means each student went back to the classroom that belonged to them.

Together, these words help organize meaning in a sentence. **“The”** points to something definite, while **“respective”** clarifies individual relationships. Though they are often overlooked, both words contribute to accuracy, structure, and understanding in English writing and speech.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention about a content recommendation system that uses display and click feedback to improve recommendations for users with little click history.
counterfactuals.output: A content recommendation system and method are disclosed for generating personalized recommendations for users having limited click history. The system collects user interaction feedback including content display events and click events, and derives training signals from both selected and non-selected displayed content. A recommendation model is trained or updated using the combined display feedback and click feedback to distinguish user interest from mere exposure, thereby reducing bias associated with sparse click data. For a target user with insufficient historical clicks, the system identifies displayed content previously presented to the user, determines engagement and non-engagement patterns, and generates a user preference representation based at least in part on the display history, click history, and similarities to other users or content items. The system then ranks candidate content items according to predicted relevance and provides recommended content to the user. By incorporating display feedback in addition to click feedback, the system improves recommendation accuracy and coverage for new or low-activity users.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a brief “present disclosure” summary describing a method, device, and system for recommending content based on average recommendation probability and user feedback including impression times and click times.
counterfactuals.output:
The present disclosure relates to a method, device, and system for recommending content to a user based on recommendation probabilities and user feedback. In one embodiment, the method includes obtaining candidate content items and determining, for each candidate content item, a recommendation probability indicating a likelihood that the user will interact with the content item. An average recommendation probability may be calculated based on recommendation probabilities associated with a plurality of content items, users, or recommendation instances.

User feedback data is collected, including impression time information indicating when recommended content is displayed to the user and click time information indicating when the user selects or interacts with the displayed content. Based on the impression times and click times, the system may determine user response behavior, such as click latency, engagement level, or whether a recommendation resulted in an effective interaction. The average recommendation probability may then be adjusted or used in combination with the feedback data to rank, filter, or select content for subsequent recommendation.

The device may include one or more processors and memory storing instructions that, when executed, cause the device to perform the recommendation method. The system may include a content server, a user terminal, and a recommendation engine configured to generate recommendation probabilities, receive user feedback including impression and click times, calculate average recommendation probabilities, and provide updated content recommendations. In this manner, the disclosed technology improves recommendation accuracy by incorporating both predictive probability information and real user interaction timing feedback.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the abstract section of a patent application for a recommendation engine that first recommends items randomly or by average probability, collects client-side display/click timing data, and then ranks preferred content accordingly.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A recommendation system and method are disclosed for ranking and presenting content items to a user based on observed client-side engagement behavior. In an initial operating state, the system selects one or more content items for display using a random selection process or based on an average probability associated with the content items. A client device presents the selected content items and records timing data associated with user interaction, including display duration, impression timing, click timing, or elapsed time between display and selection. The timing data is transmitted to a server and associated with the displayed content items. The server processes the collected timing data to determine user preference indicators for the content items and updates ranking values accordingly. In a subsequent operating state, the system ranks available content items based at least in part on the determined preference indicators and preferentially recommends content having higher ranking values. The system thereby transitions from exploratory recommendation to personalized or performance-based ranking using client-side display and click timing data.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: In formal patent language, describe a content recommendation method that determines a sequence of preferred contents from a content set using feedback information such as displaying times, displaying timing, clicking times, and clicking timing.
counterfactuals.output:
A computer-implemented content recommendation method is provided for determining a sequence of preferred contents from a content set. The method comprises acquiring, by one or more processors, a content set including a plurality of candidate contents available for presentation to a user; obtaining feedback information associated with at least a portion of the plurality of candidate contents, the feedback information including at least one of displaying times, displaying timing, clicking times, and clicking timing corresponding to respective candidate contents; determining, based on the feedback information, a preference measure for each of at least two candidate contents in the content set; and generating, according to the respective preference measures, an ordered sequence of preferred contents for recommendation to the user.

In some embodiments, the displaying times represent a number of times a corresponding content has been displayed to the user or to a group of users, and the displaying timing represents temporal information associated with one or more displays of the corresponding content, including at least one of a display time point, display duration, display interval, display frequency, or recency of display. The clicking times represent a number of times the corresponding content has been selected, activated, or clicked by the user or by the group of users, and the clicking timing represents temporal information associated with one or more clicks, including at least one of a click time point, elapsed time between display and click, click frequency, or recency of click.

The preference measure may be computed by weighting the feedback information such that content having a higher click count, a higher click-through ratio, a more recent click timing, a favorable display-to-click interval, or a favorable display timing is assigned a higher preference value. The method may further comprise normalizing the displaying times and clicking times to reduce bias caused by different exposure frequencies among the candidate contents. In one embodiment, the preference measure is determined based on a relationship between clicking times and displaying times, and is further adjusted according to a temporal attenuation factor derived from the displaying timing or the clicking timing.

The ordered sequence of preferred contents may be generated by sorting the candidate contents in descending order of the determined preference measures. The sequence may then be used to control presentation of contents on a user terminal, such that contents positioned earlier in the sequence are preferentially displayed, recommended, transmitted, cached, or otherwise made available to the user before contents positioned later in the sequence.

In certain embodiments, the method further comprises updating the feedback information in response to subsequent display events or click events, recalculating the preference measures based on the updated feedback information, and dynamically modifying the ordered sequence of preferred contents. Accordingly, the content recommendation method is capable of adaptively determining a preferred content sequence reflecting both historical user interaction and temporal characteristics of content presentation and selection.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure paragraph for improving content recommendations for random users with sparse click behavior by collecting feedback from a user client after recommending content from a content set.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed is a computer-implemented technique for improving content recommendations for users having sparse or non-representative click behavior, including random or first-time users. A recommendation service selects one or more content items from a candidate content set and transmits the selected content to a user client for presentation. After presentation, the user client collects explicit or implicit feedback associated with the recommended content, such as a rating, skip action, dwell time, scroll depth, save action, share action, dismissal, or other engagement signal, and returns the feedback to the recommendation service. The service associates the feedback with contextual information for the recommendation event, including user-session attributes, device type, content metadata, presentation position, time, and prior limited interaction history, if any. The feedback is then used to update a user preference representation, a content-item score, and/or a recommendation model configured to operate under sparse data conditions. In some embodiments, the system applies exploration logic to select diverse content from the content set, weights feedback according to confidence or signal quality, and updates future recommendations for the same user or similar anonymous users without requiring a substantial historical click profile. This enables adaptive recommendation performance for users whose prior click behavior is insufficient, random, noisy, or unavailable.
